    Rays of an algebra #

    Section 3 of that paper. Fix a complete set of primitive orthogonal idempotents e_x and put A(x, y) = e_x A e_y and R_x = e_x A e_x.

    • Definition 3.2 (def:rays): the ray of 0 ≠ f ∈ A(x, y) is the orbit [f] = {u f v : u ∈ R_x^*, v ∈ R_y^*}; U(f) = R_x f R_y and R(f) = (rad R_x) f R_y + R_x f (rad R_y).
    • Definition 3.4 (def:ray-product): M(f, h) = R_x f (rad R_y) h R_z; the ray product [f][h] is [fh] if fh ∉ M(f, h) and 0 otherwise.

    Formal choices: the units of R_x are the elements of R_x with a two-sided inverse in R_x (identity e_x); rad R_x is R_x ∩ rad A, which is the radical of R_x = e_x A e_x; subbimodules generated by sets are k-spans.

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.

                            def LargeIndecomposable.PrimitiveIdempotents.KillsZeroRayProducts {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] (F : PrimitiveIdempotents A) (b : NonzeroRay k F → A) :
                            Prop

                            The representatives b induce an algebra isomorphism k ray A ≅ A (Theorem 11.7(3)): products of representatives whose ray product is zero, that is, which lie in M(f, h), vanish. Together with a multiplicative ray transversal this says that b_r b_s = b_{rs} when rs ≠ 0 and b_r b_s = 0 otherwise.
